chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked about al-‘asabiyyah (tribal prejudice/bias), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The al-‘asabiyyah upon which its doer sins is that a man sees the evil ones of his people as better than the good ones of other people. And it is not from al-‘asabiyyah if a man loves his people, but from al-‘asabiyyah is that he assists his people upon injustice.'

key_terms.الْعَصَبِيَّةُ: Tribal prejudice or bias; the tendency to support one's group unconditionally.
key_terms.خِيَارَ: The best/good ones; plural of khayr (goodness).
key_terms.شِرَارَ: The evil/worst ones; plural of sharr (evil).
key_terms.عَلَى الظُّلْمِ: Upon injustice; the act of supporting others in their oppression or wrongdoing.
key_terms.يَأْثَمُ عَلَيْهَا: Sins upon it; the state of incurring religious guilt due to this specific type of bias.
key_terms.يُعِينَ: He assists/supports; specifically in the context of aiding in wrongdoing.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between loving one's people and sinful tribal prejudice (al-‘asabiyyah) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) distinguishes between natural tribal affection (*mawaddah*) and the sinful bias (*‘asabiyyah*) that distorts justice by prioritizing kin over merit. This definition is central to Shia ethical jurisprudence, emphasizing that loyalty becomes a vice only when it compels one to support wrongdoing, thereby linking social cohesion directly to moral integrity. The narration serves as a critical counter to pre-Islamic *Jahiliyyah* tribalism, redefing it through the lens of divine justice rather than mere bloodline.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qanasy, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Minqary, from Abdul Razzaq, from Moamar, from Al Zuhry who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the prejudice, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The prejudice upon which its doer would be sinning is that he sees the evil man of his people as better than the good ones of other people, and it is not from the prejudice if he were to love the man of his people, but from the prejudice is that he assists his people upon the injustice’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Minqari from ‘Abd al-Razzaq from Mu’ammar from al-Zuhri who has said the following: “

Once, Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was asked about racist feelings. He said, ‘The racist feeling that is a sin is the one that makes a person call the evil doers of his own people better than the virtuous individuals of the other people. A man’s loving his own people is not racism but it is a sin to help one’s own people to commit injustice.”
